input.quote: 13.4 Limitation of Liability. Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement, M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event.
input.rationale: The only cap (§ 13.4) is one-sided — it limits M&I's liability alone, leaving Customer's liability uncapped (and the Termination for Convenience/Cause Fees are expressly outside it per §§ 11.1 and 11.2(A)) — and its basis is just three months' payments, below the 6-month walk-away floor. There are no carve-outs for indemnification (§ 14.2), confidentiality (§ 17.3–17.4), gross negligence or willful misconduct; the sole exception is collection of amounts due. This fails the fallback on mutuality, quantum and carve-outs, so we have proposed the shortest fallback-level cure: make the cap mutual, move the basis to twelve months' payments, and add one carve-out sentence. The mutual consequential-damages waiver in § 13.2 is already in place. We are not re-flagging the termination fee quantum, which is addressed under the liquidated-damages rule.

proposal.summary: Make the § 13.4 cap mutual, move the basis to 12 months' payments, and place indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need the § 13.4 cap to run both ways and to sit at twelve months of payments rather than three, which is below our walk-away floor. We have also placed indemnification, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap.

ops.oldText: M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event.
ops.newText: each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months prior to the event.

ops.text: The limitation set forth in this Section 13.4 shall not apply to a party's indemnification obligations, breach of its confidentiality obligations, gross negligence or willful misconduct.

mappings.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
